raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Some scoring workloads read one shared prefix against many candidates: a cross-encoder or listwise reranker scoring one
query against N documents, or a decision model answering N questions about one state. Today each candidate is a separate
request, so the prefix is encoded N times. For encoder-only (non-causal) models prefix caching cannot help, because
bidirectional keys depend on the whole prompt.

This PR adds an opt-in **segment attention layout** for encoder-only models. The prompt is the prefix followed by the
candidates, read in one forward:

- the prefix attends to itself;
- each candidate attends to the prefix and to itself, never to another candidate;
- each candidate's positions restart right after the prefix, so it sees the positions it would see in a
  `prefix + candidate` prompt;
- the output has one row per candidate (the mean of its contextual token states).

Request it with a pooling parameter on the `token_embed` task:

```python
from vllm import LLM, PoolingParams
from vllm.pooling_params import SegmentLayoutParams

llm = LLM(
    model,
    runner="pooling",
    pooler_config={"task": "token_embed"},
    attention_backend="FLEX_ATTENTION",
)
ids = prefix_ids + [t for c in candidate_ids for t in c]
out = llm.encode(
    [{"prompt_token_ids": ids}],
    pooling_params=PoolingParams(
        segment_layout_params=SegmentLayoutParams(
            [len(prefix_ids)] + [len(c) for c in candidate_ids]
        ),
    ),
    pooling_task="token_embed",
)
# out[0].outputs.data: [num_candidates, hidden_size]
```

The online `token_embed` request takes the same field (`"segment_layout_params": {"segment_lengths": [...]}`) for
token-id prompts.

Changes:

| area | change |
|---|---|
| `vllm/pooling_params.py` | `SegmentLayoutParams(segment_lengths)`; `PoolingParams.segment_layout_params`, `token_embed` only, not with late chunking / late interaction, encoder-only models, skips prefix-cache reads |
| `vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py` | lengths must sum to the prompt length; requires the V2 model runner and `FLEX_ATTENTION` |
| `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/encoder_only.py` | per-request segment ids and restarted positions; positions passed as a model-input override, segment ids into the encoder attention metadata |
| `vllm/v1/attention/backend.py` | `CommonAttentionMetadata.encoder_segment_ids` (optional, `None` unless a request in the batch has a layout) |
| `vllm/v1/attention/backends/flex_attention.py` | encoder-only mask: same request AND (key in segment 0 OR key in the query's segment); unchanged when no layout is present |
| `vllm/model_executor/layers/pooler/tokwise/heads.py`, `special.py` | per-candidate mean pooling in the token embedding head (same path as late chunking) |
| `vllm/entrypoints/pooling/token_embed/protocol.py` | `segment_layout_params` request field |

Requests without the parameter, other attention backends, and decoder models are unaffected.

## Claims

- The layout is exact with respect to its definition: each candidate's output equals a forward of the full prompt with
  the isolating mask and restarted positions (tested against a Transformers reference with an explicit mask).
- The outputs equal N separate `prefix + candidate` forwards **only for models trained with this layout** (or whose
  prefix does not attend to later tokens). For an ordinary bidirectional encoder, a separate read lets the prefix attend
  to the candidate, which this layout does not.
- No change for requests that do not set the parameter.

## Validation

Run on an NVIDIA L40S with the vLLM nightly image for main `76c6f3f2a` and this change applied.

| test | where | result |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/attention/test_segment_attention_layout.py`: segment ids and positions, encoder mask with and without a layout, per-candidate pooling, parameter validation | CPU | 10 passed |
| `tests/models/language/pooling/test_segment_layout.py`: `sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`, FP32, 1 / 4 / 16 candidates vs a Transformers forward with the same mask and positions (atol = rtol = 2e-3) | GPU (L40S) | 3 passed |
| `tests/test_pooling_params.py`, `tests/entrypoints/pooling/token_embed/test_late_chunking.py` (existing) | CPU | passed (87 with the new file) |
| ruff check / ruff format / typos on the changed files | — | clean; full pre-commit pending |

## Benchmark

`benchmarks/benchmark_segment_layout.py`, `BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5`, BF16, `token_embed`, random token ids. Packed = one
request per group with `segment_layout_params` (FLEX_ATTENTION); separate = N `prefix + candidate` requests with the
default backend (FLASH_ATTN). Latency: median of 20 single-group reads. Throughput: 32 groups at once.

NVIDIA L40S:

| prefix x candidate tokens | N | packed latency | separate latency | packed cand/s | separate cand/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 256 x 32 | 4 | 7.0 ms | 9.0 ms | 1,735 | 974 |
| 256 x 32 | 16 | 8.9 ms | 16.2 ms | 8,897 | 1,629 |
| 256 x 32 | 64 | 9.8 ms | 48.2 ms | 10,355 | 1,737 |
| 32 x 128 | 4 | 8.7 ms | 6.5 ms | 2,838 | 2,267 |
| 32 x 128 | 16 | 8.9 ms | 11.1 ms | 3,739 | 2,589 |
| 32 x 128 | 64 | 15.7 ms | 34.6 ms | 3,887 | 2,961 |

The gain grows with the prefix share of the tokens: with a long prefix and short candidates, N = 64 is 4.9x faster per
group and 6.0x higher in candidates per second; with a short prefix it is 2.2x and 1.3x, and N = 4 is slower than
separate reads (FlexAttention vs FlashAttention for short sequences).

NVIDIA GB200 (one GPU):

| prefix x candidate tokens | N | packed latency | separate latency | packed cand/s | separate cand/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 256 x 32 | 4 | 8.0 ms | 11.8 ms | 2,534 | 2,582 |
| 256 x 32 | 16 | 10.9 ms | 15.4 ms | 10,457 | 3,506 |
| 256 x 32 | 64 | 11.9 ms | 29.0 ms | 17,223 | 4,268 |
| 32 x 128 | 4 | 10.6 ms | 9.1 ms | 3,288 | 3,291 |
| 32 x 128 | 16 | 10.9 ms | 14.4 ms | 6,763 | 4,884 |
| 32 x 128 | 64 | 12.3 ms | 22.8 ms | 8,482 | 5,360 |

On GB200, N = 64 is 2.4x faster per group and 4.0x higher in candidates per second with a long prefix, and 1.9x and
1.6x with a short prefix.

@@ -0,0 +1,166 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Benchmark segment-layout reads against separate reads.
+
+One "group" is a shared prefix and N candidates. A packed read sends the group
+as one request with ``segment_layout_params`` (one forward, FlexAttention);
+separate reads send N ``prefix + candidate`` requests. Both run on the
+``token_embed`` task of an encoder-only model and return one row per
+candidate.
+
+Reported per (prefix length, candidate length, N):
+  * latency: median wall time of one group, batch size 1;
+  * throughput: candidates per second over ``--num-groups`` groups at once.
+
+Packed prompts are longer than any single ``prefix + candidate`` prompt while
+their positions restart after the prefix, so ``--max-model-len`` may exceed
+the model's position limit; set ``VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1`` in that
+case (positions stay below ``prefix + candidate`` length).
+
+Example:
+    VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1 python benchmarks/benchmark_segment_layout.py \\
+        --model BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5 \\
+        --shapes 256x32 32x128 --num-candidates 4 16 64
+
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import gc
+import json
+import statistics
+import time
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm import LLM, PoolingParams
+from vllm.config import PoolerConfig
+from vllm.pooling_params import SegmentLayoutParams
+
+
+def make_groups(num_groups, prefix_len, cand_len, num_candidates, vocab, seed):
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+
+    def ids(n):
+        return torch.randint(1000, vocab - 1, (n,), generator=generator).tolist()
+
+    return [
+        (ids(prefix_len), [ids(cand_len) for _ in range(num_candidates)])
+        for _ in range(num_groups)
+    ]
+
+
+def packed_inputs(groups):
+    prompts, params = [], []
+    for prefix, candidates in groups:
+        prompts.append(
+            {"prompt_token_ids": prefix + [t for c in candidates for t in c]}
+        )
+        params.append(
+            PoolingParams(
+                segment_layout_params=SegmentLayoutParams(
+                    [len(prefix)] + [len(c) for c in candidates]
+                )
+            )
+        )
+    return prompts, params
+
+
+def separate_inputs(groups):
+    prompts = [
+        {"prompt_token_ids": prefix + c} for prefix, cands in groups for c in cands
+    ]
+    return prompts, [PoolingParams() for _ in prompts]
+
+
+def run(llm, prompts, params, repeats):
+    times = []
+    for _ in range(repeats):
+        start = time.perf_counter()
+        llm.encode(
+            prompts, pooling_params=params, pooling_task="token_embed", use_tqdm=False
+        )
+        times.append(time.perf_counter() - start)
+    return times
+
+
+def bench_mode(args, mode, backend, shapes):
+    llm = LLM(
+        args.model,
+        runner="pooling",
+        pooler_config=PoolerConfig(task="token_embed"),
+        attention_backend=backend,
+        max_model_len=args.max_model_len,
+        max_num_batched_tokens=args.max_num_batched_tokens,
+        max_num_seqs=args.max_num_seqs,
+        dtype=args.dtype,
+        enforce_eager=args.enforce_eager,
+        gpu_memory_utilization=args.gpu_memory_utilization,
+    )
+    vocab = llm.llm_engine.model_config.get_vocab_size()
+    build = packed_inputs if mode == "packed" else separate_inputs
+    rows = []
+    for prefix_len, cand_len in shapes:
+        for n in args.num_candidates:
+            one = make_groups(1, prefix_len, cand_len, n, vocab, seed=0)
+            many = make_groups(args.num_groups, prefix_len, cand_len, n, vocab, 1)
+            run(llm, *build(one), repeats=3)  # warm up
+            latency = statistics.median(run(llm, *build(one), args.repeats))
+            throughput = run(llm, *build(many), repeats=3)
+            rows.append(
+                {
+                    "mode": mode,
+                    "backend": backend,
+                    "prefix_len": prefix_len,
+                    "candidate_len": cand_len,
+                    "num_candidates": n,
+                    "latency_ms": round(latency * 1e3, 2),
+                    "candidates_per_s": round(
+                        args.num_groups * n / statistics.median(throughput), 1
+                    ),
+                }
+            )
+            print(json.dumps(rows[-1]), flush=True)
+    del llm
+    gc.collect()
+    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
+    return rows
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--model", default="BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--shapes",
+        nargs="+",
+        default=["256x32", "32x128"],
+        help="PREFIXxCANDIDATE token lengths",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--num-candidates", type=int, nargs="+", default=[4, 16, 64])
+    parser.add_argument("--num-groups", type=int, default=32)
+    parser.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=20)
+    parser.add_argument("--max-model-len", type=int, default=16384)
+    parser.add_argument("--max-num-batched-tokens", type=int, default=65536)
+    parser.add_argument("--max-num-seqs", type=int, default=256)
+    parser.add_argument("--dtype", default="bfloat16")
+    parser.add_argument("--gpu-memory-utilization", type=float, default=0.8)
+    parser.add_argument("--enforce-eager", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--separate-backends",
+        nargs="+",
+        default=["FLASH_ATTN", "FLEX_ATTENTION"],
+        help="attention backends for the separate-reads baseline",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--output-json", default=None)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    shapes = [tuple(int(x) for x in s.split("x")) for s in args.shapes]
+    rows = bench_mode(args, "packed", "FLEX_ATTENTION", shapes)
+    for backend in args.separate_backends:
+        rows += bench_mode(args, "separate", backend, shapes)
+    if args.output_json:
+        with open(args.output_json, "w") as f:
+            json.dump(rows, f, indent=2)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""GPU: a segment-layout read (one forward for a shared prefix and several
+candidates) matches a reference forward with the same isolating mask and
+restarted positions."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm import PoolingParams
+from vllm.config import PoolerConfig
+from vllm.pooling_params import SegmentLayoutParams
+
+MODEL = "sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2"
+
+
+def _reference_means(hf_model, prefix: list[int], candidates: list[list[int]]):
+    """HF forward with the segment mask and positions, then the mean of each
+    candidate's token states."""
+    ids = prefix + [t for c in candidates for t in c]
+    lengths = [len(prefix)] + [len(c) for c in candidates]
+    segment = torch.cat(
+        [torch.full((n,), k, dtype=torch.long) for k, n in enumerate(lengths)]
+    )
+    mask = (segment.view(1, -1) == 0) | (segment.view(-1, 1) == segment.view(1, -1))
+    positions = torch.cat(
+        [torch.arange(len(prefix))]
+        + [torch.arange(len(prefix), len(prefix) + len(c)) for c in candidates]
+    )
+    device = next(hf_model.parameters()).device
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        out = (
+            hf_model(
+                input_ids=torch.tensor([ids], device=device),
+                # 4D additive mask: used as is by the attention layers.
+                attention_mask=torch.zeros(
+                    1, 1, len(ids), len(ids), device=device
+                ).masked_fill(~mask.to(device), torch.finfo(torch.float32).min),
+                position_ids=positions.unsqueeze(0).to(device),
+                token_type_ids=torch.zeros(
+                    1, len(ids), dtype=torch.long, device=device
+                ),
+            )
+            .last_hidden_state[0]
+            .float()
+        )
+    rows = out[len(prefix) :].split(lengths[1:])
+    return torch.stack([r.mean(dim=0) for r in rows]).cpu()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_candidates", [1, 4, 16])
+def test_segment_layout_matches_masked_reference(vllm_runner, num_candidates):
+    from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer
+
+    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL)
+    prefix = tokenizer("which city is the capital of france?")["input_ids"]
+    candidates = [
+        tokenizer(f"document {k}: paris has {k} famous bridges.")["input_ids"][1:]
+        for k in range(num_candidates)
+    ]
+    hf_model = (
+        AutoModel.from_pretrained(MODEL, attn_implementation="eager")
+        .to(torch.float32)
+        .cuda()
+        .eval()
+    )
+    expected = _reference_means(hf_model, prefix, candidates)
+
+    ids = prefix + [t for c in candidates for t in c]
+    layout = SegmentLayoutParams([len(prefix)] + [len(c) for c in candidates])
+    with vllm_runner(
+        MODEL,
+        runner="pooling",
+        pooler_config=PoolerConfig(task="token_embed"),
+        dtype="float32",
+        attention_backend="FLEX_ATTENTION",
+        enforce_eager=True,
+        max_model_len=256,
+    ) as vllm_model:
+        outputs = vllm_model.llm.encode(
+            [{"prompt_token_ids": ids}],
+            pooling_params=PoolingParams(
+                use_activation=False, segment_layout_params=layout
+            ),
+            pooling_task="token_embed",
+            use_tqdm=False,
+        )
+    got = outputs[0].outputs.data.float().cpu()
+    assert got.shape == expected.shape
+    torch.testing.assert_close(got, expected, atol=2e-3, rtol=2e-3)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Segment attention layout: segment ids/positions, the FlexAttention encoder
+mask, the per-candidate pooler and request validation (CPU)."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.exceptions import VLLMValidationError
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.pooler.tokwise.heads import _mean_pool_segments
+from vllm.pooling_params import PoolingParams, SegmentLayoutParams
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends import flex_attention
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.flex_attention import FlexAttentionMetadata
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_states.encoder_only import segment_layout_rows
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.cpu_test
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def _cpu_doc_ids(monkeypatch):
+    """Build the request lookup on the CPU (the backend stages it on the GPU)."""
+
+    def doc_ids(query_start_loc_cpu, device):
+        counts = query_start_loc_cpu[1:] - query_start_loc_cpu[:-1]
+        return torch.repeat_interleave(torch.arange(len(counts)), counts)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(flex_attention, "_offsets_to_doc_ids_tensor", doc_ids)
+
+
+def test_segment_layout_rows():
+    segment_ids, positions = segment_layout_rows([3, 2, 4])
+    assert segment_ids.tolist() == [0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2]
+    # Each candidate restarts right after the 3-token prefix.
+    assert positions.tolist() == [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 3, 4, 5, 6]
+
+
+def _encoder_mask(query_start_loc: list[int], segment_ids: list[int] | None):
